A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Pathryoshka, with matching methods, teachers and experiments. All supplied pages are readable. However, v1 includes supplementary material, whereas v2 ends at the bibliography and references unavailable supplementary Tables S1, S4 and S6, limiting the appendix comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, efficiency and ablation results, including additional experiments in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds GPFM comparisons, teacher-representation analysis and ConSep/MoNuSAC segmentation results.

M1.justification: The documented procedure retains the same teachers, aligned and non-aligned crops, nested embedding prefixes, projection heads and cosine/MSE losses. Explicit equal teacher weighting in v2 clarifies the existing unweighted sums. The new evaluation heads do not establish a change to Pathryoshka itself.

E1.justification: v2 adds segmentation on ConSep and MoNuSAC, extending evaluation from classification and retrieval to spatial mask prediction. The original internal training dataset, ten classification benchmarks and CCRCC retrieval task remain.

E2.justification: GPFM becomes an evaluated multi-teacher pathology baseline in the classification, efficiency, retrieval and nested-embedding comparisons. These corresponding v1 experiments included the teachers and H0-mini but not GPFM. Its citation in v1 did not constitute an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include Dice-based segmentation with a convolutional decoder receiving patch tokens and raw images, and CKA analysis on 10,000 training images with DINOv2 reference controls. UNI2-h's k-NN evaluation extends to dim/128, while the PCA visualization tests truncation through dim/256. The shared classification and throughput protocols remain unchanged as documented.

E4.justification: v2 adds teacher-complementarity analysis using CKA and quantitative segmentation tests under embedding truncation, while expanding k-NN compression analysis from three to six existing classification datasets. The cropping ablation is retained and moved from v1 Table 7 to v2 Table 3. A new single-teacher ablation is summarized, but its cited Table S6 is unavailable.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 adds one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across datasets, reporting p-values of 0.042, 0.010 and 0.019 against UNI2-h, H0-mini and GPFM. This adds an inferential layer while retaining the existing five-run reporting and 500-batch throughput statistics; increased repetition counts are not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPFM scores, segmentation results, CKA measurements and additional k-NN results. Examples include GPFM's median classification score of 80.3 and Pathryoshka-B's ConSep Dice scores of 63.6 at full dimensionality and 62.6 at dim/16. Existing classification and Recall@5 entries are largely retained with rounding. Table 2 changes Pathryoshka-B throughput from 885.1 ± 7.1 to 842 ± 4 images/s under the same stated measurement protocol.

T1.justification: The main nested-embedding definitions and loss equations are mathematically equivalent; v2 additionally numbers an existing head-mapping equation. However, v1's appendix includes an O(nd) k-NN runtime argument, whose retention or revision cannot be checked because v2's supplementary material is unavailable.

C1.justification: The four central contributions and 86-92% model-compression claim remain. v2 extends the abstract's superiority claim to multi-teacher distillation through a reported 5.3-point advantage over GPFM, qualifies the earlier novelty positioning, and strengthens deployment language to describe the model as already suited for clinical settings.

C2.justification: v2 adds a CKA-based explanation of teacher complementarity and flags training/evaluation overlap for relevant baseline results. Its rewritten discussion no longer contains v1's explicit single-institution/scanner and correlated-teacher-bias limitations, while asserting clinical suitability and interpreting compression as evidence that large models underutilize their capacity. These substantially alter the qualifications and implications presented to readers.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-weights location, explicit equal teacher weighting and segmentation-head information. v1's implementation section specifies eight GPUs, batch size 1024, AdamW, 300,000 iterations, learning-rate and decay schedules, and EMA evaluation; these details are unavailable in v2. Its missing supplement prevents determining whether this substantial reproducibility information was relocated or lost.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the assertion that multi-teacher distillation had not been explored in pathology with explicit discussion of GPFM, positioning Pathryoshka around compression relative to larger teachers and nested embeddings. GPFM was already cited in v1, but this substantive relationship was absent. Related work also expands discussion of unsupervised distillation, teacher-head accessibility and embedding efficiency.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the method subsections, moves teacher selection into Methodology, and extensively rewrites related work and the discussion. The standalone implementation section disappears from the supplied main text, while author information, terminology and explanatory passages are revised.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting. Figure 4 becomes six separate panels with uncertainty bars and absolute embedding sizes; Figure 5 uses a different tissue example and stronger truncation. Other diagrams are revised, Table 2 is transposed, the cropping table moves into the main text, and a segmentation table is added.

improvement.justification: GPFM comparisons, segmentation validation, significance tests and more accurate prior-work positioning strengthen v2. However, the supplied version lacks v1's detailed training recipe and its own referenced supplement, while replacing explicit limitations with stronger clinical-suitability language without corresponding clinical validation. These material benefits and losses, together with unavailable supplementary evidence, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
